assessment.nobel_worthiness: Turning the ubiquitin-proteasome machinery into a chemically programmable tool: heterobifunctional degraders and molecular glues convert a biological process into defined chemistry (induced proximity, ternary-complex formation) and give biologists and medicine a general way to remove proteins. Originality and breadth are high, and the thalidomide-cereblon mechanism links directly to disease and clinical practice.
assessment.attribution: Crews and Deshaies conceived and first demonstrated the PROTAC concept; Ciulli supplied VHL ligands and the structural/mechanistic basis of ternary complexes. The thalidomide/cereblon molecular-glue arm (Handa, Ito, Gray and others) is a competing claim, so a three-person prize leaves a fair credit boundary unresolved.
assessment.maturity: Strong independent confirmation across many labs and E3 ligases, and degraders are in late-stage clinical trials, though approval-level clinical validation is still pending. Timing is plausible rather than premature.
uncertainties: Whether the prize should centre on PROTACs or on molecular glues/cereblon, and who is credited for each.
Clinical benefit of degraders is not yet established by an approved drug, as far as I know (not independently verified).

assessment.nobel_worthiness: Base editing converts one base to another through programmed chemistry on DNA (cytidine and adenine deaminases fused to a Cas nickase) without double-strand breaks. It is an elegant chemical solution to a biological problem, with a very wide tool-user community and direct therapeutic relevance to genome maintenance and repair.
assessment.attribution: David R. Liu led the conceptual design and the evolution of the adenine base editor; Komor and Gaudelli were first authors and key contributors but a single-laureate proposal is the cleanest configuration and keeps the CRISPR-adjacent allocation simple. Kondo and Nishida's parallel cytidine-deaminase work is an unresolved credit question.
assessment.maturity: Replicated widely; first clinical-stage data exist. Off-target and bystander editing remain studied issues that I would want quantified with careful measurement. Recognition is timely given the 2020 CRISPR prize precedent.
uncertainties: Overlap with the 2020 genome-editing prize may make the committee view this as incremental.
Priority between Liu's and Nishida/Kondo's work on deaminase-based editing.

assessment.nobel_worthiness: Massively parallel sequencing-by-synthesis rests on reversible-terminator nucleotide chemistry and clonal amplification on surfaces, a chemical advance that transformed genomics and medicine. Impact is enormous and enduring, and the chemistry is clear and general.
assessment.attribution: Balasubramanian and Klenerman founded the Solexa chemistry; Mayer's colony-sequencing and parallel-clonal approach is a distinct and important origin. Other credits (Rothberg for pyrosequencing-based 454, Ju for reversible terminators) complicate a clean three-person prize.
assessment.maturity: Fully mature, with decades of independent use and cost reduction; recognition would not be premature.
uncertainties: Competing technology lineages (454, Illumina, Ju's terminators) make allocation contentious.
Whether the committee sees this as chemistry or as genomics technology.

assessment.nobel_worthiness: Quantitative mass-spectrometry proteomics turned measurement of cellular protein content into a routine analytical chemistry capability, including quantification of modifications, with broad biomedical use. As someone who values properly quantified measurements, I weigh this highly, but the field is a broad ensemble of methods.
assessment.attribution: Mann (high-resolution quantitative MS and SILAC-style proteomics), Aebersold (targeted and SRM/SWATH-type approaches) and Yates (shotgun proteomics, MudPIT) made distinct decisive contributions. Hunt, Gygi and Heck are also credited, so three is a compromise.
assessment.maturity: Mature and independently confirmed, with long-standing routine use. Part of the area was recognised by the 2002 mass-spectrometry prize, which could lower priority.
uncertainties: Overlap with the 2002 Nobel for biomolecular mass spectrometry.
Which of several methods is the discrete discovery being honoured.

assessment.nobel_worthiness: Reading nucleic acids as ionic current through a single pore turns sequencing into a direct electrical chemical measurement, with long reads and direct detection of modified bases including RNA modifications. Original and with clear practical impact.
assessment.attribution: Deamer, Akeson and Branton's early strand-translocation work, Kasianowicz's pore demonstration, and Bayley's engineered pores and enzyme-based approach together underlie the field. A three-person list omits Branton and Kasianowicz, so allocation is an open issue.
assessment.maturity: Commercially deployed and independently validated, though accuracy for some applications is still improving and the field has recently matured rather than long settled.
uncertainties: Credit split among five people with overlapping priorities.
Relative importance of pore engineering versus enzyme-controlled translocation.

assessment.nobel_worthiness: Ionizable lipid nanoparticles are the chemical delivery system that made RNA therapeutics and mRNA vaccines practical, an enabling chemistry with demonstrated population-scale impact. The lipid chemistry and pKa-driven endosomal escape mechanism are well defined.
assessment.attribution: Cullis led the lipid nanoparticle formulation and ionizable-lipid concept, with MacLachlan, Madden and Hope as key co-contributors; Anderson and Langer contributed lipidoid libraries. Because the 2023 Medicine prize honoured mRNA modifications, credit here is chiefly delivery chemistry, and the three-person selection excludes several important people.
assessment.maturity: Validated at scale clinically by independent products; the mechanism of endosomal escape is still being refined.
uncertainties: Credit among Cullis, MacLachlan, Madden, Hope and the Langer/Anderson group is disputed.
Possible perception of overlap with the 2023 Medicine prize.

assessment.nobel_worthiness: Reversible m6A methylation defines a new chemical layer of RNA regulation with writers, erasers and readers, linking RNA modification chemistry to development, cancer and metabolism. Conceptually important, though I would want to see disciplined quantitative work behind several mechanistic claims.
assessment.attribution: He's group identified the FTO demethylase as an eraser and the broader reversible system; Jaffrey and Rechavi mapped m6A transcriptome-wide. Jia, Yang, Dominissini and Meyer also hold major credit, so allocation is unsettled.
assessment.maturity: Replication is broad, but some map-level and mechanistic details remain under debate, e.g. m6A-site specificity, mapping artefacts and disagreement over specific reader functions; recognition may be somewhat early.
uncertainties: Disagreement about mapping resolution and method-specific artefacts.
Unclear whether the prize should honour the eraser, the mapping or the whole system.

assessment.nobel_worthiness: Phosphoramidite chemistry made solid-phase automated DNA synthesis routine and underpins primers, PCR, sequencing, gene synthesis and oligonucleotide therapeutics. It is a clear chemical invention with huge lasting impact and mature, undisputed value.
assessment.attribution: Caruthers developed the phosphoramidite method and is the central figure; Hood's role was in instrumentation and automation, which makes a single laureate the cleanest proposal.
assessment.maturity: Fully mature, with decades of use, which also means the long delay and loss of some of the original contributors can make recognition less likely.
uncertainties: The committee may regard it as a past-era achievement overshadowed by later nucleic-acid technology.
Extent of the contribution of automation (Hood) versus the chemistry.
